# EMPYEMA/LUNG ABSCESS

Empyema is usually a complication of pneumonia. Diagnostic thoracentesis is recommended in most cases. Pulmonary or Infectious Diseases consultation is recommended.

____________________________________________

## Inpatient 

## Duration

The duration of antibiotic therapy for bacterial empyema is not well-defined but generally 4-6 weeks.

____________________________________________

References: 
Harrison's chapter: Infections due to mixed organisms
Up-to-date article: Epidemiology, clinical presentation, and diagnostic evaluation of parapneumonic effusion and empyema in adults
Sanford Guide article: Empyema, Adult, Child > 5 yrs
Therapy:
## Inpatient

Ampicillin-Sulbactam 3 mg IV q6h [M]
< OR >
Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q24h [M]
< OR >
Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q24h [M] <AND> metronidazole 500 mg PO q12h [DI]

Suspected MRSA:
< ADD > vancomycin 15mg/kg IV q12h [R] to an antimicrobial regimen above

## Oral Step down

Preferred:
Amoxicillin-clavulanate 875-125 mg PO q12h [R]
<OR>
Cefadroxil 1000 mg PO q12h [R]
<OR>
Cefadroxil 1000 mg PO q12h [R] <AND> metronidazole 500 mg PO q12h [DI]

Alternative:
[Assessment of Beta-lactam Reaction](beta-lactam-allergy-assessment)
Levofloxacin 750 mg PO q24h [R,DI]
< OR >
Levofloxacin 750 mg PO q24h [R,DI] <AND> metronidazole 500 mg PO q12h [DI]

## Outpatient

Refer to Inpatient Antimicrobial CDSS.
